Theorem 2 gives the PT asymptotic law, Theorem 3 gives the SC asymptotic law, the corresponding influence functions and asymptotic variances may differ, and Theorem 4 establishes multiplier-bootstrap consistency under either theorem's assumptions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(1\le g\le J+1\), \(p_X(x)>\kappa_0\), \(p_g(x)\in(\epsilon_0,1-\epsilon_0)\), \(\max_{g,t}E_{P_{0,O}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]<M_4\), \(\lambda_{\min}\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}>\kappa_0\), every nonzero eigenvalue of \(\Omega_x\) is greater than \(\kappa_0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_x)\) is locally constant, profiling \(q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x)\) over the unrestricted path of \(\delta_1^0(x)\) yields the observed normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\) for \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\). Its Gram rank is at most \(J-1\), with equality under positive definiteness on the donor-contrast range. The SC normal Gram rank is at most \(T-J\), with equality under positive definiteness on the residualized complement of \(\operatorname{col}B(x)\). For either branch, \[\mathcal T_b(P_0)=\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{b,x}s]=0\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\},\] and \[\dot\theta_b(s)=E_{P_{0,O}}\!\left[\left\{\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}\right\}s\right],\qquad \mathcal I_b(P_0)=\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.\] Consequently, \[\phi_b=\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}-R_b^{\prime}\{E_{P_{0,O}}[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\}^{\dagger}E_{P_{0,O}}\!\left[R_b\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}\right],\] and \(V_b=E_{P_{0,O}}[\chi_b^2]\) plus the minimum variance of the centered branch face. Redundant displayed rows are handled by the Moore--Penrose inverse.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The two-sided exponential-tilt converse can leave a weak inequality boundary. Strict slack in every probability, moment, SC-spectrum, and nonzero-normal-spectrum margin, together with locally constant rank, is therefore required at the theorem point.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(1\le g\le J+1\), \(p_X(x)>\kappa_0\), \(p_g(x)\in(\epsilon_0,1-\epsilon_0)\), \(\max_{g,t}E_{P_{0,O}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]<M_4\), \(\lambda_{\min}\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}>\kappa_0\), every nonzero eigenvalue of \(\Omega_x\) is greater than \(\kappa_0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_x)\) is locally constant, the common class \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\) is nonempty, and every estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) has asymptotic variance at least \(V_U(P_0)=E_{P_{0,O}}[\phi_U^2]\). At the intersection, \(C_{\mathrm{PT}}(x)=C_{\mathrm{SC}}(x)\) and hence \(\chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0\). If \((a_x^U,d_x^U)\) solves \(\mathrm{QP}_x\), then \[\phi_U=\chi_0+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}=\chi_0+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\},\] and \[V_U(P_0)=E_{P_{0,O}}[\chi_0^2]+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_X(x)\min\mathrm{QP}_x.\] Relative to the alternative-hypothesis laws for the one integrated estimator in SunXieZhang2025, this is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark at the stated strict-interior constant-rank intersection law for procedures regular under PT-or-SC uncertainty. It neither replaces the branch-specific asymptotic variances, furnishes an implemented standard error, nor proves attainment or multiplier validity.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The tangent-normal result on which the envelope rests is valid for two-sided local paths only at strict-interior constant-rank theorem points; the comparison wording must also describe the cited integrated estimator exactly.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(1\le g\le J+1\), \(p_X(x)>\kappa_0\), \(p_g(x)\in(\epsilon_0,1-\epsilon_0)\), \(\max_{g,t}E_{P_{0,O}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]<M_4\), \(\lambda_{\min}\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}>\kappa_0\), every nonzero eigenvalue of \(\Omega_x\) is greater than \(\kappa_0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_x)\) is locally constant, simultaneous oracle adaptation holds if and only if the observable simultaneous Gram discrepancy in \(\mathrm{def{:}oracle\text{-}gram\text{-}tests}\) is zero; equivalently, \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\) if and only if \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\) in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\). One-sided PT adaptation \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}\) holds if and only if the PT-oracle Gram discrepancy is zero, and one-sided SC adaptation \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\) holds if and only if the SC-oracle Gram discrepancy is zero. These are finite covariance-matrix tests in \(\Omega_x\), \(a_x^{\mathrm{or}}\), and \(d_x^{\mathrm{or}}\), all identified from the observed law.

The full-rank SC observed model is therefore locally nested in the PT observed model, \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\), \(\phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\), and \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}\). With \(T=2\), this PT gradient equals the panel-DiD ATT efficient influence function in SantAnnaZhao2020, Proposition 1(a), equation (2.11), whose efficiency bound is equation (2.12).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: When \(J=T\), at every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(1\le g\le J+1\), \(p_X(x)>\kappa_0\), \(p_g(x)\in(\epsilon_0,1-\epsilon_0)\), \(\max_{g,t}E_{P_{0,O}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]<M_4\), \(\lambda_{\min}\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}>\kappa_0\), every nonzero eigenvalue of \(\Omega_x\) is greater than \(\kappa_0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_x)\) is locally constant, each \(B(x)\) is square and invertible, the profiled SC restriction is identically zero, and \(R_{\mathrm{SC},x}\) has rank zero. Therefore \[\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)=\mathcal H_{P_0},\qquad \mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\},\] and \[\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\},\qquad \phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}},\qquad V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}.\]

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose the constructed law \(P^{\star}\) has strict fourth-moment slack, \[\max_{1\le g\le3}\max_{1\le t\le3}E_{P_O^{\star}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]<M_4,\] and choose the fixed margins so that \(1>\kappa_0\), \(1/3\in(\epsilon_0,1-\epsilon_0)\), every nonzero eigenvalue of the displayed \(\Omega\) is greater than \(\kappa_0\), and its rank is locally constant. Then the corrected PT vector is \(q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=(0,0)^{\prime}\), its profiled normal has rank one, and \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\); moreover \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\prime}B)=2>\kappa_0\). The uniquely identified SC weights are \((1/2,1/2)\), while minimizing the PT Gram criterion over donor weights summing to one gives \((4/5,1/5)\). The exact efficiency bounds are \[V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{42}{5},\qquad V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{1625}{184},\qquad V_U(P^{\star})=\frac{39}{4},\] with gaps \[V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{27}{20},\qquad V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{169}{184}.\] The union QP fixes the final donor coefficients at \((1/2,1/2)\); its required SC preperiod-normal coefficient differs from the SC oracle coefficient, so both one-sided Gram discrepancies are strictly positive. The same strict inequalities hold on a relatively open region preserving strict fourth-moment slack, full rank, the stated nonzero-spectrum and locally constant-rank margins, unequal positive donor-change variances, and unequal SC and PT-oracle weights.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Efficiency-bound and adaptation language requires the witness itself to lie in the repaired strict-interior constant-rank scope; in particular, the weak fourth-moment inequality must be made strict.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Under the frozen definition of \(\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\), the requested uniform asymptotic-linear conclusion, and hence the requested four-part affirmative attainment result, is false in general. In particular, take \(P_0=P^{\star}\) and fixed margins for which the witness has strict slack in cell mass, two-sided group overlap, fourth moments, the SC spectrum, every nonzero normal eigenvalue, and the positive local-score variance bound, with locally constant displayed ranks. For every sufficiently small nonzero \(\delta\), let \(Q_\delta\) retain the donor means and innovation laws of \(P^{\star}\) but replace the treated untreated mean path by \((-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta)\), and define \[\Delta_\delta=\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})-\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star}).\] Then \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and \[E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]\ge\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.\] For every sample size, finite-coordinate splicing produces two elements of \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\) having the same observed law at that coordinate but different admissible chart labels. No single estimator can have both chart expansions uniformly. This obstruction proves no affirmative sequencewise continuation theorem; it merely does not rule out such a theorem after imposing a common local neighborhood, common bounds on the QMD scores and remainders, and exclusion of arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The obstruction must be centered at a witness admitted with strict slack in every margin, including the fourth-moment and local-score variance margins, so that the perturbed laws remain in the frozen class.

prose_updates.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification is valid on the union of conditional parallel trends and a full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction. At strict-interior, locally constant-rank intersection points, the corrected derivative separates the common treated-composition gradient \(\chi_0\) from conditionally centered stratum gradients. Their affine-class intersection and union convolution lower bound are computed by finite covariance-weighted programs, with \(E[\chi_0^2]\) added to the envelope and both oracle variances; observable Gram discrepancies characterize simultaneous and one-sided adaptation. The exact strict three-group witness and the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoints remain valid on this repaired scope. Sun, Xie, and Zhang analyze one integrated ATT estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction under alternative PT and SC hypotheses, with branch-specific influence functions and variances. This paper adds a sharp local lower-bound benchmark, not implemented inference; finite-coordinate splicing makes the requested uniform attainment theorem false over the frozen sequence class.

project_justification.gap: SunXieZhang2025 identifies the ATT under alternative PT and SC hypotheses and analyzes one integrated estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction: Theorems 2 and 3 give branch-specific influence functions and asymptotic variances that may differ, and Theorem 4 proves bootstrap consistency under either theorem's assumptions. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives PT efficiency alone. Neither source determines the common regular influence class or union convolution bound at strict-interior constant-rank PT--SC intersection points.
project_justification.niche: Finite covariate support turns each branch into finitely many conditional-mean restrictions. At strict-interior constant-rank theorem points, separating \(\chi_b\) from \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\) restores the product rule; the common \(\chi_0\) is orthogonal to the centered restriction geometry, so the local efficiency loss and adaptation frontier are computable from observed conditional covariance Grams.
project_justification.fill: The project derives corrected PT and SC affine influence classes at strict-interior locally constant-rank intersection points, solves their centered intersection by stratum covariance-weighted quadratic programs, and adds \(E[\chi_0^2]\) to the union and oracle variances. It proves simultaneous and one-sided oracle criteria, the strict three-group region, and both endpoint reductions. The lower-bound and impossibility conclusions apply to estimators regular on the broader published union by restriction to this subclass, while sharpness is local to the repaired subclass. No implemented standard error or uniform multiplier theorem is delivered.

Sun, Xie, and Zhang's one integrated estimator has alternative PT and SC asymptotic representations. This paper proves no cross-fitted projection estimator, variance estimator, data-driven chart coupling, or multiplier procedure valid over the frozen local-sequence class.

prose_updates.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor and analyzes one integrated ATT estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction under alternative assumptions. Its PT condition is the donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. Its SC hypothesis uses covariate-indexed weights common across periods, summing to one with negative weights allowed and \(T\ge J\); the intercept row of \(B\) encodes the sum constraint. Its identification theorem need not identify weights uniquely, while its SC estimation theorem assumes a uniformly nonsingular reference-donor difference system equivalent, after reparameterization, to full column rank of augmented \(B\). Theorems 2 and 3 give the PT and SC asymptotic laws for the integrated estimator, with influence functions and variances that may differ, and Theorem 4 gives multiplier-bootstrap consistency under either theorem's assumptions. The present model is a finite-support, uniform-margin, full-rank subclass, and the new sharpness claim is local to strict-interior constant-rank points in that subclass. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting but not the nonnested union geometry. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different union model. SantAnnaZhao2020, Proposition 1(a), equation (2.11), supplies the panel-DiD influence function, and equation (2.12) supplies its efficiency bound; equation (2.13) is for repeated cross-sections. Newey1990, Sections 2--3, supports the generic regular-estimator efficiency lower bound, while Newey1994 is retained only for its separately verified constant-rank role. NeweyRobins2018, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016, and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 are guidance for a possible repaired uniform theorem. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer by restriction to estimators regular over the broader published union; RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska analysis in SunXieZhang2025 receive a benchmark, not a new standard-error procedure.
prose_updates.interpretation: At a strict-interior constant-rank intersection law, the cost of requiring regularity under either identifying restriction is the squared-distance cost of forcing the PT and SC affine influence faces to agree. The common treated-composition term does not affect that distance but does contribute \(E[\chi_0^2]\) to every variance. A zero Gram discrepancy means local robustness is free in the specified direction; a positive discrepancy is a local efficiency cost, not an estimated diagnostic with its own sampling theory.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected union envelope is a local regularity lower bound only at strict-interior intersection laws with locally constant rank and strict support, moment, SC-spectrum, and nonzero-normal-spectrum slack. Its common treated-composition component is identified analytically, but no attaining estimator, usable standard error, or multiplier-confidence procedure is established. The negative theorem uses a witness with strict slack, including in the local-score variance margin, and depends on the frozen sequence class's closure under arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements. It does not settle a redesigned common neighborhood with common QMD-score and remainder bounds. Boundary overlap, saturated moment inequalities, rank changes, covariance degeneracy, and weight restrictions require different local experiments.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved deliverables are strict-interior, locally constant-rank versions of the corrected tangent-normal characterization \(\mathcal I_b=\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}R_b\), the finite centered union convolution lower bound with \(E[\chi_0^2]\), observable oracle-adaptation tests, the exact strict three-group witness, and the single-donor and saturated-donor reductions. Sun, Xie, and Zhang supply one integrated estimator and one multiplier construction analyzed under alternative PT and SC hypotheses; this paper preserves that integrated-construction description and provides no new implemented inference. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer to estimators regular on the broader published union by restriction to the repaired subclass, while sharpness remains local to that subclass. The frozen sequence class makes a uniformly chartwise expansion false by finite-coordinate splicing, and no positive sequencewise continuation theorem is claimed.
